Yes, I agree that machines are smarter than humans and they can do things faster than humans but I think that there's more to life than just doing things fast and efficiently. There being a mixture of two sides will be a good aspect, but realistically I think it is very hard to mix both aspects and not make one side more biased. I agree more towards the dystopian view than the other two views. ", '', 'My perspective is more similar to dystopian view in the sense that we lose humanity, intentionality, and emotions when we start replacing humans with machines. The more you don\'t interact with people, the more you lose that skill and ability to interact with others. For example during COVID years, we had to be isolated from others which allowed us to be comfortable with just ourselves. This also led to the terms of "COVID babies" where the children weren\'t able to interact with others during those times where they learn how to socialize and talk with others that they didn\'t know how to talk to each other when they started going back to school or starting going to things in person. In that terms, replacing machines with humans will allow there to be an increase in efficiency but will decrease a lot of the social aspects that are needed in life to live. ', '']

I agree more towards the dystopian view than the other two views. ", '', 'My perspective is more similar to dystopian view in the sense that we lose humanity, intentionality, and emotions when we start replacing humans with machines. The more you don\'t interact with people, the more you lose that skill and ability to interact with others. For example during COVID years, we had to be isolated from others which allowed us to be comfortable with just ourselves. This also led to the terms of "COVID babies" where the children weren\'t able to interact with others during those times where they learn how to socialize and talk with others that they didn\'t know how to talk to each other when they started going back to school or starting going to things in person. In that terms, replacing machines with humans will allow there to be an increase in efficiency but will decrease a lot of the social aspects that are needed in life to live. ', '', 'The relationship that my perspective has with the utilitarian view is that there is an understanding of efficiency being put as a priority. However, this perspective disregards emotions and social aspects and only focuses on the aspects of work. There are a lot of workaholics with this type of view because they emphasis the importance of getting things done quickly.
